# Implementing MVC ToDo App with NestJS – Comprehensive Learning Guide

## Course Overview

This course teaches you how to build a full-featured ToDo application using **NestJS**, a progressive Node.js framework that implements the **MVC (Model-View-Controller)** architectural pattern. You'll learn server-side JavaScript/TypeScript best practices, REST API design, database integration, and enterprise-level code organization.

**Who This Is For:**
- JavaScript developers transitioning to backend development
- Engineers preparing for full-stack or backend Node.js interviews
- Those seeking to understand structured, scalable application architecture
- Developers wanting to master TypeScript in a real-world context

**Why It Matters for Interview Prep:**
- NestJS is used at companies like Google, Microsoft, and Airbnb for production systems
- Demonstrates understanding of design patterns (MVC, dependency injection, middleware)
- Shows ability to build RESTful APIs with proper error handling and validation
- Proves familiarity with TypeScript, decorators, and modern JavaScript
- Signals knowledge of testing, documentation, and professional code organization

---

## Core Topics Covered

- **NestJS Fundamentals** – Controllers, providers, modules, and dependency injection
- **MVC Architecture** – Separating concerns into Models, Views (API responses), and Controllers
- **TypeScript Essentials** – Type safety, interfaces, decorators, and generics in practice
- **RESTful API Design** – HTTP methods, status codes, request/response handling, validation
- **Database Integration** – TypeORM, entity relationships, migrations, and queries
- **Middleware & Guards** – Authentication, authorization, error handling, and logging
- **Testing & Documentation** – Unit tests, integration tests, and API documentation (Swagger)
- **Deployment Patterns** – Environment configuration, build optimization, production best practices

---

## Learning Path Workflow

### **Phase 1: NestJS & TypeScript Fundamentals (Tasks 1–15)**

**Objective:** Understand NestJS structure and core concepts.

1. Install NestJS CLI and scaffold your first project
2. Understand the module system and how modules interact
3. Create your first controller and handle GET requests
4. Learn the provider pattern and dependency injection
5. Create services and inject them into controllers
6. Understand decorators (`@Controller`, `@Get`, `@Body`, etc.)
7. Handle POST, PUT, DELETE requests in a controller
8. Create request DTOs (Data Transfer Objects) and understand validation
9. Create response DTOs for consistent API responses
10. Implement basic error handling with HttpException
11. Create custom exception filters
12. Understand the middleware pattern
13. Implement logging middleware
14. Create a global error handling strategy
15. **Task 15:** Build a basic controller with CRUD endpoints (no database yet)

---

### **Phase 2: Database Integration & MVC Models (Tasks 16–30)**

**Objective:** Connect your app to a database and implement the Model layer.

16. Set up TypeORM and connect to PostgreSQL/MySQL
17. Create your first entity (ToDo model)
18. Understand entity relationships and decorators
19. Generate and run database migrations
20. Create a repository pattern wrapper service
21. Implement CREATE operations with TypeORM
22. Implement READ (GET all, GET by ID) operations
23. Implement UPDATE operations with proper validation
24. Implement DELETE operations
25. Handle database constraints and validation errors
26. Create database seeders for testing data
27. Implement query filtering and sorting
28. Add pagination to list endpoints
29. Handle transactions in complex operations
30. **Task 30:** Build complete CRUD API for ToDo items with database persistence

---

### **Phase 3: Advanced Features & Best Practices (Tasks 31–50)**

**Objective:** Add professional-grade features to your application.

31. Implement JWT authentication strategy
32. Create a sign-up endpoint with password hashing (bcrypt)
33. Create a login endpoint returning JWT tokens
34. Implement auth guards to protect routes
35. Add user roles and permissions system
36. Create middleware to extract user from JWT token
37. Implement refresh token strategy
38. Add request validation using class-validator
39. Create custom validators for domain logic
40. Implement global validation pipes
41. Add comprehensive error messages and logging
42. Create custom decorators for common patterns
43. Implement caching strategies
44. Add rate limiting to prevent abuse
45. Implement soft deletes for ToDo items
46. Add timestamps (createdAt, updatedAt) to entities
47. Create audit logging for important operations
48. Implement batch operations (bulk update/delete)
49. Add filtering by user and status
50. **Task 50:** Add authentication and authorization to your ToDo API

---

### **Phase 4: Testing, Documentation & Polish (Tasks 51–70)**

**Objective:** Test, document, and prepare for production.

51. Write unit tests for services using Jest
52. Mock dependencies in unit tests
53. Write integration tests for controllers
54. Test error scenarios and edge cases
55. Achieve >80% code coverage
56. Set up Swagger/OpenAPI documentation
57. Document all endpoints with proper descriptions
58. Add example request/response payloads to Swagger
59. Document authentication requirements
60. Create comprehensive API documentation
61. Implement request logging middleware
62. Add structured logging with Winston or Pino
63. Implement performance monitoring
64. Create health check endpoint
65. Set up environment-based configuration
66. Add validation for environment variables
67. Optimize database queries with eager loading
68. Create database indexes for performance
69. Implement graceful shutdown handling
70. **Final Task 70:** Deploy your complete ToDo app and write deployment documentation

---

## Key Skills You'll Build

### **Architecture & Design**
- Implement MVC pattern in production code
- Apply dependency injection for testability and maintainability
- Design clean, scalable module structures
- Understand separation of concerns

### **Backend Development**
- Build RESTful APIs with proper HTTP semantics
- Handle asynchronous operations in Node.js
- Manage database relationships and queries
- Implement authentication and authorization flows

### **TypeScript Mastery**
- Write type-safe code with generics and interfaces
- Use decorators effectively
- Understand advanced TypeScript patterns
- Leverage type checking for bug prevention

### **Professional Practices**
- Write testable, maintainable code
- Document APIs comprehensively
- Handle errors gracefully
- Implement security best practices
- Optimize performance with caching and indexing

### **Problem-Solving**
- Debug complex multi-layer issues
- Balance performance with maintainability
- Make architectural trade-offs
- Refactor code for clarity and efficiency

---

## Sample Problem Types

### **Problem Type 1: Building CRUD Endpoints with Validation**

**Description:** Create a complete CRUD API for ToDo items with request validation and proper error handling.

**Code Sketch:**

```typescript
// src/todos/dto/create-todo.dto.ts
import { IsString, IsNotEmpty, MaxLength, MinLength } from 'class-validator';

export class CreateTodoDto {
  @IsString()
  @IsNotEmpty()
  @MinLength(3)
  @MaxLength(255)
  title: string;

  @IsString()
  description?: string;
}

// src/todos/todos.controller.ts
import { Controller, Get, Post, Body, Param, Put, Delete, HttpCode } from '@nestjs/common';
import { TodosService } from './todos.service';
import { CreateTodoDto } from './dto/create-todo.dto';

@Controller('todos')
export class TodosController {
  constructor(private readonly todosService: TodosService) {}

  @Get()
  findAll() {
    return this.todosService.findAll();
  }

  @Get(':id')
  findOne(@Param('id') id: string) {
    return this.todosService.findOne(+id);
  }

  @Post()
  @HttpCode(201)
  create(@Body() createTodoDto: CreateTodoDto) {
    return this.todosService.create(createTodoDto);
  }

  @Put(':id')
  update(@Param('id') id: string, @Body() updateTodoDto: CreateTodoDto) {
    return this.todosService.update(+id, updateTodoDto);
  }

  @Delete(':id')
  @HttpCode(204)
  remove(@Param('id') id: string) {
    return this.todosService.remove(+id);
  }
}
